1988: "The predecessor of DW-TV was RIAS-TV, a television station launched by RIAS, a West Berlin broadcaster in August 1988."
1990: "The fall of the Berlin Wall the following year and German reunification in 1990 led to the closure of RIAS-TV."

1992: "On 1 April 1992, Deutsche Welle inherited RIAS-TV's broadcast facilities, using them to start a German and English-language television channel broadcast via satellite, DW (TV), adding a short Spanish broadcast segment the following year."
1995: "In 1995, it began 24-hour operation (12 hours in German, 10 hours in English, two hours in Spanish)."
2001: "In 2001, Deutsche Welle (in conjunction with ARD and ZDF) founded a subscription TV channel for North American viewers called German TV."
2009: "In March 2009, DW-TV expanded its television services in Asia with two new channels: DW-TV Asia and DW-TV Asia+."
2015: "Deutsche Welle changed its schedules again on 22 June 2015, with DW in Asia and Oceania and DW (Europe) merged to become a 24-hour English news channel."

2020: "In the U.S., some of its programs were distributed via the World Channel as well as MHz Worldview, although after the closure of MHz Worldview in 2020, a few stations have since offered a full carriage of DW-TV."
2009: "In August 2009, DW-TV ceased broadcasts on Sky channel 794 in the United Kingdom."
2014: "To the Point (formerly Quadriga) Agenda (Discontinued in December 2014)"
"The project was shut down after four years due to low subscriber numbers."
"English programmes on DW (Arabia) and DW (Español) were discontinued."
2012: "Deutsche Welle relaunched their television channels and their schedules on 6 February 2012, using the abbreviation DW for all its services."
